'''Star Wars World Championships''' is a special report by [[Michael Mikaelian]] in ''[[InQuest]]'' #22 (February 1997, page 14). Mikaelian covered the [[1996 Decipher World Championship]] of 7–9 December 1996 at the Vail Cascade Hotel and Club in Vail, Colorado.<ref name="inquest">Michael Mikaelian, "Star Wars World Championships", ''InQuest'' #22 (February 1997), p. 14. Scan: [https://archive.org/details/inquest-magazine-issue-22 InQuest Magazine Issue 22], Internet Archive.</ref>

[[File:InQuest 22 page 14.jpg|thumb|right|260px|InQuest #22, February 1997, page 14.]]

<blockquote>
'''SPECIAL REPORT'''<br />
'''Star Wars World Championships'''

''Photo caption: Michael Mikaelian (left) at the Star Wars worlds. Photo courtesy of Decipher.''

''Editor's Note: [[Michael Mikaelian]] of Brooklyn, N.Y., author of InQuest #20's "Killer Decks II" [[Michael Mikaelian Yavin 4 Counterstrike|Yavin 4 Counterstrike]] deck for Star Wars, qualified to play in the Star Wars: Customizable Card Game world championships Dec. 7-9, 1996, at the Vail (Colo.) Cascade Hotel and Club. He filed this report after completing the hyperspace jump back home.''

It was snowing when I arrived on Hoth.

Most people think of Colorado as, well, Colorado. Not Decipher, to whom Colorado is the ice world of Hoth from George Lucas' "Star Wars."

Thirteen of the 38 competitors were stranded on the road for five hours while safety workers conducted avalanche control above the Vail Pass—the only road between Denver and Vail—but even the wintry weather the Friday night before the tournament started didn't prevent everyone from arriving in time. (But why aren't the snowspeeders ever ready when you need 'em?)

The championships began Saturday morning with two-player matches. Competition was stiff: Many of the world's top 20 Star Wars CCG players were there. In the first round, my opponent was [[Joe Alread]], whom I'd defeated in the finals of the [[1996 GenCon Open|Gen Con]] Star Wars tourney. Joe's {{CardLink|X-wing|X-Wings}} knew {{CardLink|A Few Maneuvers}}, and every time we battled, I lost half of my forces. Joe ended up squeaking out a three-Force (three-card) victory, thus avenging his earlier loss to me.

After each match, point totals (two for a win, one for a tie, none for a loss) and Force differentials were totaled, and each player was assigned a new opponent with similar ratings. Everyone was friendly, I noticed: Players wished one another luck before each game and congratulated opponents afterward for putting up a good fight.

My second opponent was [[Rusty Zion]]. Every time he tried to block my Force drains, my {{CardLink|Jawa|Jawas}} manhandled his spies. I surprised the Empire by hitching a few rides with {{CardLink|Nabrun Leids}} ("Game Breakers," InQuest #20), and {{CardLink|Obi-Wan Kenobi|Obi-Wan}} said {{CardLink|Sorry About The Mess}} en route to my five-card victory.

When the day was done, my earlier opponents had finished in the top 12—Joe ranked first, in fact—and advanced to Sunday's finals. Me? I came in 29th (hey, somebody had to!).

Sunday's competition started at 9 a.m. with random pairings. It ended up coming down to a championship match between Norwegian [[Bjørn Sørgjerd|Bjorn Sorgjerd]] and Canadian [[Raphael Asselin]].

In the first of two games, Sorgjerd, playing the Dark Side, used {{CardLink|Darth Vader}} and {{CardLink|Grand Moff Tarkin}} to coordinate guerrilla tactics on Tatooine. {{CardLink|Mosep}}, a very annoying Dark Side alien, was effective against Asselin's all-space deck. Asselin was forced to discard Obi-Wan from the top of his deck, and Sorgjerd continued to a nine-card win.

In game two, Asselin deployed an intimidating fleet of {{CardLink|Imperial-Class Star Destroyer|Imperial Star Destroyers}} and used {{CardLink|Scanning Crew}} to survey Sorgjerd's hand. Before long, Asselin's ships were draining his opponent's Force at every system on the table. Sorgjerd's attempt to control the surface of Tatooine was crushed by the Star Destroyers.

After the {{CardLink|Millennium Falcon}} was destroyed with all hands aboard, including {{CardLink|Han Solo}}, Sorgjerd said, "It is a dark time for the Rebellion." Realizing that Asselin would win and that the championship would come down to a two-game Force-differential tie-breaker, Sorgjerd attempted to reduce Asselin's Force to nine or less.

But when the Light Sider succumbed, Asselin had enough to claim the championship.

His prize: a plaque and an all-expenses-paid trip to Tunisia, including a visit to the remnants of George Lucas' Mos Eisley Cantina and Lars homestead film sets from the original "Star Wars."

—[[Michael Mikaelian]]
